title: ZIdentity list filters on the wire: key spelling, [like] matching and list values

prose.text: The filter names are generated with each list operation; what matters here is how each client spells them on the wire. {{contract-keys}}

prose.label: Python.
prose.text: {{python-docstring-keys}} {{python-params-camel-cased}} {{python-camel-rule}} {{python-wire-keys}} The Python keys therefore differ from the contract's {{divergence:filter-key-spelling}}, and whether the server accepts them anyway is open {{gap:filter-key-case}}. {{python-contract-spelling-passes}}

prose.label: List-valued filters.
prose.text: The contract and Go encode several login names, domains or identity providers differently {{divergence:array-encoding}}.

checks.do: Whether a Python filter on users or groups was passed with the contract's spelling (`loginname`, `excludedynamicgroups`) rather than the SDK docstring's snake_case, which goes out camel-cased.

contract-keys.statement: The contract spells the user filters in run-together lowercase (`loginname`, `loginname[like]`, `displayname[like]`, `primaryemail[like]`, `domainname`, `idpname`) and the group filter as `excludedynamicgroups`; `name[like]` filters API clients, groups and resource servers.

expect.description: Excludes dynamic groups from the results.
Filters results by one or multiple login names.

go-keys.statement: The Go SDK sets the query keys `excludedynamicgroups`, `loginname`, `loginname[like]`, `displayname[like]`, `primaryemail[like]`, `domainname`, `idpname` and `name[like]`, written with the brackets in the key string.

python-docstring-keys.statement: The Python SDK's docstrings name the filters in snake_case: `login_name`, `login_name[like]`, `display_name[like]`, `primary_email[like]`, `domain_name` and `idp_name` for users, and `exclude_dynamic_groups` for groups.

python-params-camel-cased.statement: The Python request executor classifies any URL containing `/ziam/admin/api/v1` as the `ziam` service, and for every service other than ZPA it camel-cases the query parameter keys.

quotes: # Normal param conversion if not ZPA

python-camel-rule.statement: The camel-casing helper returns a key from its exceptions table as mapped and leaves a key without an underscore unchanged; otherwise it splits on underscores, lowercases the first part, capitalizes every later part and joins them.

quotes: if not string or "_" not in string:

python-wire-keys.statement: So a Python caller using the docstring names sends `loginName`, `loginName[like]`, `displayName[like]`, `primaryEmail[like]`, `domainName`, `idpName` and `excludeDynamicGroups`; only `name[like]`, `offset` and `limit` go out as the contract spells them.
python-wire-keys.conditions: Follows from applying the helper's rule to the docstring keys; none of these keys appears in the exceptions table at the pin (searched).

python-contract-spelling-passes.statement: A Python caller can send the contract's spelling by passing it as the key (`loginname`, `excludedynamicgroups`), since a key without an underscore is not changed.
python-contract-spelling-passes.conditions: Follows from the helper's rule; not exercised by an SDK test or example.

like-descriptions.statement: The contract describes the user (`loginname[like]`, `displayname[like]`, `primaryemail[like]`), group and resource-server `[like]` filters as case-insensitive partial matches, but the API-client `name[like]` only as a partial match.

filter-key-spelling.summary: The contract and Go spell the user and group filters in run-together lowercase, while the Python SDK, called with its documented snake_case names, sends camelCase keys.

positions.says: The query keys are `excludedynamicgroups`, `loginname`, `domainname`, `idpname` and the lowercase `[like]` forms.

quotes: ``[query_params.exclude_dynamic_groups]`` {bool}: Excludes dynamic groups from the results.

positions.says: Python documents `exclude_dynamic_groups`, which its executor sends as `excludeDynamicGroups`.

filter-key-spelling.impact: If the server matches query keys exactly, a Python filter written as documented is ignored and the call returns the unfiltered list, with no error; a Go call and a raw call following the contract filter as intended.

array-encoding.summary: For list-valued filters the contract sets `explode` to false, which in OpenAPI's default form style means one comma-separated value, while the Go SDK repeats the key once per value.

positions.says: `loginname` (and `domainname`, `idpname`) is an array parameter with `explode` false.
Go adds one `loginname` (or `domainname`, `idpname`) pair per value.

array-encoding.impact: With more than one value, a server that follows the contract may read only one of Go's repeated keys, and a server that expects repeated keys may read a comma-separated value as one name. A single value is sent the same way by both.

filter-key-case.title: Whether the ZIdentity API accepts camelCase or snake_case filter keys
filter-key-case.detail: Unverified legacy statement: a raw-HTTP caller may send either Python's camelCase keys (`loginName`, `excludeDynamicGroups`) or Go's run-together keys. Only the run-together spelling is in the contract; no capture shows how the server treats the camelCase keys Python sends.
